checks: The base sum consists of independent symmetric signed differences and has an even continuous density. Its positive and negative half-transforms satisfy A(−t)=B(t) on the symmetric admissible interval. Therefore the convex reciprocal H is even and H(t)≥H(0)=4, giving G(t)≤1/4.

The coordinate means scale by their positive tilted rates. Their full product scales by Z, and the tilt identity writes the cap variance as ZG. Thus strictness for k≥2 follows from strictness of the base product, independently of whether H itself is strictly convex.

For k=1, direct Laplace integration gives the two half-transforms 1/[2(1∓p_1t)]. Their reciprocal sum is four, so both inequalities are equalities. Zero coefficients contribute independent coordinates of mean one.
Every conditional coordinate mean is positive. Dividing by an omitted factor at most one only increases the full product.

Forward reciprocal identities follow by inversion. The harmonic-mean formula and the common difference give both reciprocal identities in reverse, and positivity of both recovered rates gives the strict open-interval condition for each pair.
The frozen :6 and :5 source sections match the product inequality and coefficient-only characterization, respectively.
